Senior Dimensional Engineer — Product Development
Hybrid, Toronto preferred
Metafold | Hybrid, Toronto preferred

Metafold is building a fundamentally better way to do tolerance analysis. We’re looking for a seasoned dimensional engineer to join a team with deep expertise in geometry, mathematics, and software—and bring practical tolerance analysis expertise to the development of exceptional engineering tools.

You’ll contribute directly to product development, work closely with customers, and represent Metafold in technical conversations throughout the sales cycle. This role suits someone who combines strong engineering judgment with the ability to present clearly, build relationships, and get people working toward a shared goal.
You’ll bring dimensional engineering expertise to a collaborative product team, applying experience from real products and production environments to next-generation tolerance analysis software.
Contribute to product direction: bring a practitioner’s judgment to product priorities, workflows, and capabilities, working closely with our geometry and software teams.
Lead technical work: perform and review tolerance and variation analyses, investigate dimensional issues, and recommend practical design or process improvements.
Validate performance: develop representative engineering cases, assess modeling assumptions, and evaluate results against established methods and measurement data.
Build customer relationships: understand engineering challenges, lead productive technical discussions, and translate customer feedback into actionable insights.
Support the sales cycle: deliver compelling demonstrations and presentations, scope technical evaluations, and explain the engineering and business value of Metafold’s approach.
Substantial professional experience in dimensional engineering, geometry assurance, or mechanical engineering with significant responsibility for tolerancing and variation analysis.
A record of independently resolving dimensional problems in product development and production. You can explain the decisions you made and the results they delivered.
Practical understanding of manufacturing processes, inspection data, and process capability.
Proficiency with CAD software and experience working with mechanical parts and assemblies.
Working knowledge of FEA and engineering simulation software, including model setup, assumptions, boundary conditions, and interpretation of results.
Excellent presentation and interpersonal skills. You can lead a room, communicate complex ideas clearly, and build credibility with engineers, managers, and prospective customers.
A collaborative approach: you listen carefully, share knowledge, welcome constructive challenge, and take responsibility for shared outcomes.
This is a senior role requiring demonstrated field experience applying dimensional engineering methods to real products. Coursework and certifications should be supported by practical experience.
A degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Electronics or electromechanical product experience, particularly connectors, enclosures, precision assemblies, or electronics packaging.
Experience improving engineering tools or workflows, or collaborating with software development teams.

This is a hybrid position, with a preference for candidates based in Toronto. We will also consider strong candidates elsewhere in Canada, with working arrangements discussed during the hiring process.
Introductory interview: discuss your experience, interests, and what you’re looking for, and learn about Metafold and the role.

“We really identified this bottleneck at the design side,” said Ross. “There are hardware manufacturers who have these factories of 3D printers, and they’re ready to manufacture things, but there aren’t enough people designing things for 3D printing, because it’s hard.”
As Active Impact founder and managing partner Mike Winterfield puts it, Metafold aims to provide “missing middleware” to connect traditional design software to 3D printers.

“There’s lots of great design software out there, there’s actually greatly improved hardware out there … but there isn’t an easy way to get your designs from traditional software over to that hardware,” Winterfield told BetaKit in an interview.
Metafold sees potential in targeting manufacturers using 3D printing to manufacture “frontier technologies” in the cleantech, aerospace, and medical sectors.

Ross expressed excitement about having Active Impact as a backer, describing the firm as “a great fit” for Metafold due to its cleantech focus, and the expertise it brings on the sales and fundraising fronts, given Metafold’s particularly technical founding team.

Ross emphasized Metafold’s expertise in lattices and metamaterials as a differentiator. The CEO also highlighted that unlike Metafold’s offering—which manufacturers can integrate into their existing tools—other available products are often tied to specific pieces of hardware.

Ultimately, Ross is bullish on the long-term potential of combining manufacturing with a focus on geometry. “I think 3D printing will be impactful on the lives of everyone through these kinds of frontier technologies that are under development now,” she said. “I’m just excited to be supporting people who are pushing these boundaries.”

Metafold 3D is a Toronto-based B2B SaaS startup that drives new applications for industrial 3D printing through its cloud-native Design for Additive Manufacturing platform. Metafold helps engineers develop remarkable new products in aerospace, medical, automotive and consumer goods, and bring those products to market more quickly than leading alternatives.
